certificate.description:
TLS certificate for the server, issued by cert-manager. Kanidm REQUIRES TLS: it
terminates TLS itself for both HTTPS and LDAPS, so the certificate cannot be terminated
at an ingress or load balancer. The issued secret is mounted read-only into the pod at
/certs (tls.crt as the chain, tls.key as the key). cert-manager's tls.crt already has
the leaf certificate first, matching Kanidm's chain.pem format.

annotations.description: Additional annotations for the Certificate resource.
annotations.title: annotations

commonName.description: The common name of the certificate. Defaults to the Kanidm domain.
commonName.title: commonName

dnsNames.description:
Subject alternative names of the certificate. Defaults to the Kanidm domain, which
MUST be covered by the certificate.
dnsNames.title: dnsNames

enabled.description:
Create a cert-manager Certificate resource. Disable to bring your own secret via
`kanidm.tls.existingSecret`.
enabled.title: enabled

group.description: API group of the issuer resource.
group.title: group

name.description: Name of the cert-manager Issuer or ClusterIssuer (required when certificate.enabled).
name.title: name

labels.description: Additional labels for the Certificate resource.
labels.title: labels

encoding.description: Key encoding; Kanidm accepts an unencrypted PKCS1 or PKCS8 PEM key.
encoding.title: encoding

rotationPolicy.description: "Always" generates a new key on every renewal; "Never" reuses the key.
rotationPolicy.title: rotationPolicy

size.description:
Key size in bits: 2048/4096 for RSA, 256/384/521 for ECDSA. Kanidm requires at
least 2048-bit RSA or 224-bit ECDSA keys.
size.title: size

renewBefore.description: How long before expiry the certificate should be renewed.
renewBefore.title: renewBefore

secretName.description: The name of the secret to create. Defaults to "{{ include "kanidm.fullname" . }}-tls".
secretName.title: secretName

secretTemplate.description: Labels and annotations propagated onto the managed TLS secret.

annotations.description: Annotations to add to the managed TLS secret.
annotations.title: annotations

labels.description: Labels to add to the managed TLS secret.
labels.title: labels

secretTemplate.title: secretTemplate

usages.description: Extended key usages for the certificate. Kanidm only needs "server auth".
usages.title: usages

certificate.title: certificate

env.description:
Extra environment variables for the server container. Use these (or `envFrom`) to
inject secrets as `KANIDM_`-prefixed environment variables, which take precedence over
the server.toml rendered from the `kanidm` values below.
env.title: env

extraVolumeMounts.description: Additional volume mounts for the server container.
extraVolumeMounts.title: extraVolumeMounts

extraVolumes.description: Additional volumes mounted into the server container.
extraVolumes.title: extraVolumes

fullnameOverride.description: This is to override the release fullname.
fullnameOverride.title: fullnameOverride

global.description: Global values are values that can be accessed from any chart or subchart by exactly the same name.
global.title: global

digest.description:
Optional image digest. When set, it is used instead of the tag and pins the image
content immutably (recommended for production deployments).
digest.title: digest

tag.description: Overrides the image tag whose default is the chart appVersion.
tag.title: tag

imagePullSecrets.description:
Secrets for pulling the image from a private repository, see
https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/pull-image-private-registry/
imagePullSecrets.title: imagePullSecrets

ingress.description:
Kanidm terminates TLS itself (it is required for both HTTPS and LDAPS), so the ingress
must pass TLS through to the pod instead of terminating it. For ingress-nginx, enable
ssl-passthrough cluster-wide (--enable-ssl-passthrough) and keep the default
annotations below. For Traefik, use the `ingressRouteTCP` section instead.

annotations.description:
Annotations for the ingress. The defaults assume ingress-nginx with ssl-passthrough
enabled; adjust for other controllers.
annotations.title: annotations

host.description: Host to route. Defaults to the Kanidm domain.
host.title: host

ingress.title: ingress

ingressRouteTCP.description: Traefik TCP routing (IngressRouteTCP, traefik.io/v1alpha1; requires the Traefik Kubernetes CRDs). Like the nginx ingress, Traefik must pass TLS through to the pod un-terminated.

enabled.description: Create an IngressRouteTCP for the HTTPS interface.
enabled.title: enabled

labels.description: Additional labels for the IngressRouteTCP resource.
labels.title: labels

annotations.description: Additional annotations for the IngressRouteTCP resource.
annotations.title: annotations

entryPoints.description: Traefik entry points receiving the HTTPS traffic.
entryPoints.title: entryPoints

match.description: TCP match rule; HostSNI(`*`) passes every TLS connection on the entry points through. Restrict it (e.g. HostSNI(`idm.example.com`)) on shared entry points.
match.title: match

tlsPassthrough.description: Delegate TLS termination to the backend (Kanidm); keep true.
tlsPassthrough.title: tlsPassthrough

middlewares.description: TCP middlewares, e.g. [{name: my-ip-allow-list, namespace: traefik}].
middlewares.title: middlewares

ldaps.description: Route the LDAPS interface as well (requires `kanidm.ldap.enabled`).

enabled.description: Create an IngressRouteTCP for the LDAPS interface.
enabled.title: enabled

entryPoints.description: Traefik entry points receiving the LDAPS traffic.
entryPoints.title: entryPoints

match.description: TCP match rule for the LDAPS route.
match.title: match

middlewares.description: TCP middlewares for the LDAPS route.
middlewares.title: middlewares

ldaps.title: ldaps

ingressRouteTCP.title: ingressRouteTCP

kanidm.description:
Kanidm server configuration, rendered into the server.toml ConfigMap. Only the most
common options are exposed; append anything else verbatim via `kanidm.extraConfig`.

bindAddress.description: The HTTPS bind address inside the pod; the container port is 8443.
bindAddress.title: bindAddress

clientAddressInfo.description:
How client IP addresses are discovered when traffic is reverse proxied. Only one
method may be configured per listener. Leave everything empty when the service is
exposed directly (LoadBalancer / NodePort).

proxyProtocolV2.description:
IPs or CIDRs allowed to supply the PROXY protocol v2 header to the HTTPS
listener.
proxyProtocolV2.title: proxyProtocolV2

xForwardedFor.description:
IPs or CIDRs allowed to supply X-Forwarded-For to the HTTPS listener. Upstream
discourages this: prefer PROXY protocol v2.
xForwardedFor.title: xForwardedFor

proxyProtocolV2.description:
IPs or CIDRs allowed to supply the PROXY protocol v2 header to the LDAPS
listener.
proxyProtocolV2.title: proxyProtocolV2

clientAddressInfo.title: clientAddressInfo

arcSize.description:
Number of entries to store in the in-memory cache (minimum 256). Unset uses an
automatic heuristic; only tune this if you experience memory pressure.
arcSize.title: arcSize

fsType.description:
Tune the database page size to the backing filesystem: "zfs" sets a 64K page size
(requires recordsize=64k on the dataset), "other" uses 4K. Leave empty for the
default; changing it requires running a vacuum task.
fsType.title: fsType

domain.description:
The DNS domain name of the server. Used in security-critical contexts (WebAuthn,
OAuth2, SPNs), so it MUST match the hostname users reach the server on, and the TLS
certificate must be issued for it. Changing it later breaks registered credentials
and requires `kanidmd domain rename`.
domain.title: domain

extraConfig.description:
Raw TOML appended to the generated server.toml, for options the chart does not model.
Note that top-level keys must come before any [table] header, so use tables here.
extraConfig.title: extraConfig

bindAddress.description: The LDAPS bind address inside the pod.
bindAddress.title: bindAddress

enabled.description: Enable the read-only LDAP-over-TLS interface; the container port is 3636.
enabled.title: enabled

path.description: Output directory of the online backups, on the data volume.
path.title: path

schedule.description:
Cron schedule of the online database backup task (see https://crontab.guru/).
Backups are written below `kanidm.onlineBackup.path` on the data volume. Set to ""
to disable the task.
schedule.title: schedule

versions.description: Number of online backups to keep.
versions.title: versions

origin.description:
The origin for WebAuthn and OAuth2: the URL users visit, with the port included only
when it is non-standard (anything except 443). Must match or be a descendant of
`domain`. Defaults to https://<kanidm.domain>.
origin.title: origin

otelGrpcUrl.description:
OpenTelemetry OTLP/gRPC endpoint for trace exports, e.g.
http://otel-collector.observability:4317. Allow egress to the collector through
`networkPolicy.additionalEgress`.
otelGrpcUrl.title: otelGrpcUrl

existingSecret.description:
Name of an existing TLS secret (with tls.crt and tls.key entries) to mount instead
of the one issued by `certificate`. Required when `certificate.enabled` is false.
existingSecret.title: existingSecret

kanidm.title: kanidm

livenessProbe.description: Restarts the container when /status stops responding. Set to null to remove.
livenessProbe.title: livenessProbe

nameOverride.description: This is to override the chart name.
nameOverride.title: nameOverride

networkPolicy.description:
Network policy. Kanidm is the root of trust for the whole network ("game over" if it is
compromised), so the default policy allows ingress from any source on the service ports
and denies all egress except cluster DNS. Use `additionalEgress` to reach an in-cluster
OpenTelemetry collector or other dependencies.

additionalEgress.description:
Additional egress rules appended to the policy, e.g. for an OpenTelemetry collector:

  additionalEgress:
    - to:
        - namespaceSelector:
            matchLabels:
              kubernetes.io/metadata.name: observability
      ports:
        - protocol: TCP
          port: 4317
additionalEgress.title: additionalEgress

enabled.description: Create a NetworkPolicy for the server pod.
enabled.title: enabled

networkPolicy.title: networkPolicy

persistence.description:
Persistence for the Kanidm database (and its online backups). Expect up to 8KB of disk
per database entry.

annotations.description: Annotations to add to the claim.
annotations.title: annotations

enabled.description: Create a persistent volume claim for /data.
enabled.title: enabled

existingClaim.description: Use an existing claim instead of creating one. Must be writable by fsGroup.
existingClaim.title: existingClaim

storageClass.description:
Storage class of the claim; leave empty to use the cluster default. Flash storage
(NVMe) is strongly recommended.
storageClass.title: storageClass

persistence.title: persistence

podAnnotations.description: Annotations to set on the pod.
podAnnotations.title: podAnnotations

podDisruptionBudget.description:
Pod disruption budget. Kanidm is a single-instance service, so a PDB cannot preserve
availability; it is disabled by default.

enabled.description: Create a PodDisruptionBudget for the server pod.
enabled.title: enabled

maxUnavailable.description: Maximum number of pods that may be unavailable after a voluntary disruption.
maxUnavailable.title: maxUnavailable

minAvailable.description:
Minimum number of pods that must be available after a voluntary disruption. With a
single replica use 0, or use `maxUnavailable` instead.
minAvailable.title: minAvailable

podDisruptionBudget.title: podDisruptionBudget

podLabels.description: Labels to set on the pod.
podLabels.title: podLabels

podSecurityContext.description:
Satisfies the "restricted" Pod Security Standard together with the container
securityContext. The fsGroup must own the database volume so the server (uid 1000) can
manage its files in /data.
podSecurityContext.title: podSecurityContext

priorityClassName.description: Priority class name for the pod.
priorityClassName.title: priorityClassName

readinessProbe.description: Removes the pod from the Service endpoints while /status is failing, so clients are not routed to a wedged instance. Set to null to remove.
readinessProbe.title: readinessProbe

resources.description:
Container resource requirements. Kanidm trades memory for throughput: budget roughly
64KB of RAM per database entry plus headroom.
resources.title: resources

securityContext.description:
Hardened container context. Kanidm only ever writes to /data (the database volume), so
the root filesystem can stay read-only and no privileges are required: the server binds
8443/3636 inside the pod, never ports below 1024.
securityContext.title: securityContext

annotations.description: Annotations for the service (e.g. cloud provider or MetalLB configuration).
annotations.title: annotations

externalTrafficPolicy.description:
External traffic policy for NodePort and LoadBalancer services. "Local" preserves the
client source IP.
externalTrafficPolicy.title: externalTrafficPolicy

httpsPort.description:
Service port for the HTTPS interface (web UI, APIs, OIDC); the container listens on
8443.
httpsPort.title: httpsPort

ldapsPort.description:
Service port for the LDAPS interface; the container listens on 3636. Only used when
`kanidm.ldap.enabled` is true.
ldapsPort.title: ldapsPort

type.description:
Service type. ClusterIP suits an ingress doing TLS passthrough; use LoadBalancer to
expose the server directly.
type.title: type

annotations.description: Annotations to add to the service account.
annotations.title: annotations

create.description:
Specifies whether a service account should be created. Kanidm never talks to the
Kubernetes API; token mounting is disabled either way.
create.title: create

name.description:
The name of the service account to use. If not set and `create` is true, a name is
generated using the fullname template.
name.title: name

startupProbe.description: Startup probe. Grants up to failureThreshold * periodSeconds (5 minutes by default) for database checks and recovery on large databases before the liveness probe takes over. Set to null to remove.
startupProbe.title: startupProbe

terminationGracePeriodSeconds.description: Time for in-flight requests and the online backup to finish on shutdown.
terminationGracePeriodSeconds.title: terminationGracePeriodSeconds
